questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose the destination because I love the Italian culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The most amazing experience. Would recommend it to everyone.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The Erasmus coordinator was fast in his replies.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much assistance was given in the beginning, but if you asked for help yourself, you would get it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing part is usually quite hard in Milano- I shared an apartment with some other Danish students close to campus, and it was a very nice apartment. My advice is to start looking at housing very early - we found an apartment almost 6 month before arrival.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The same as above.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process at the host institution was easy and simple. If in doubt just contact the office and they will help you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Information was not really given advance - therefore you had to seek for information yourself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses that I wanted, and so did everyone I know.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont stress about the registration part. You have several weeks to try out all courses to decide which courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level differed when it comes to the different courses. Some courses required more than others. In my opinion the level was lower compared to the level at UCPH, and it was very easy to understand the teachers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a very different style of teaching - more class participation, no group work, no breaks during classes, etc.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Negotiation, mediation and sustainable conflict resolution. Gender Justice. International, European and comparative environmental law. AI, law issue and sustainability. Law and policies on social rights protection in Europe.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The teacher in Law and policies on social rights protection in Europe was amazing. I learned a lot in International, European and comparative environmental law, but it was a bit boring. AI, law issue and sustainability was a very interesting course, but the teacher was a but confusing at times with no clear structure. Gender Justice was a fun and interesting course, but the teacher was very "unfriendly" and many students were "scared" to say something during class.Negotiation, mediation and sustainable conflict resolution was a very useful course, but the workload was huge, and you have to prepare 2 simulations during the semester as well as participate in a oral exam with both teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Milan is the most expensive city in Italy. A lot of things are cheaper than in Denmark, but it surprised my that grocery shopping was as expensive (and sometimes more expensive) than in Danmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee, dining out, public transport, etc. was less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not participate in these.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in Italy - I went to so many beautiful places. Get aperitivo and eat pasta every day.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in Italy and see cities like Verona, Como, Venice, Bergamo, Torino, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy for me, as I love the Italian laid back culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find anything particular hard. But the Italians eat dinner very late, which I struggled to adopt to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, wine, laidback culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Enjoy your stay while it last. 2. Socialize with locals. 3. Focus on having fun and making memories for life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I met and the trips I went on. I loved every single day in Milan.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I didnt find anything particular challenging.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
